data.content_ref: inline:The target commits an is-ought fallacy: it explicitly reduces the preference to 'a description of survival' (a purely descriptive relation) yet concludes that the preference is 'defensible' and 'rational' (normative claims). With both the premises and derivation arrays empty, no bridging premise is supplied to license the move from 'this theory survived' to 'therefore preferring it is rational.' The mechanism's assertion that preference is 'rational because it is the only one left standing' merely relabels the descriptive fact of survival as rationality without any justificatory premise. This is exposed by the countercondition the target itself lists — 'the extinction of all current theories leaves no basis for preference' — which concedes that survival alone can fail to ground preference, undermining the generality of the normative conclusion.
